synopsis: For detection trials with misses, the booklet recommends Clopper-Pearson exact binomial intervals or another pre-declared binomial interval, rather than continuing testing until a desirable percentage appears [f5452, f6891, f14196]. Clopper-Pearson is described as exact and conservative, making it the safe default for regulators; Wilson is a less conservative alternative that behaves better at moderate sample sizes [f6892, f6893, f14211]. The detection sample-size table allows one or two failures using what the text calls a Poisson or Clopper-Pearson approximation, leaving a terminology tension with the description of Clopper-Pearson as exact [f6884, f6892]. These are mature, non-automotive-specific statistical techniques, but their direct applicability requires respecting independence, representative sampling and homogeneous-rate assumptions [f7398, f7399].
